title: Energy insecurity separates household sacrifice, public reach, restoration, and durable recovery
source_unit: Deliberately non-pooled comparison of EIA RECS housing-unit consequences, LIHEAP program aggregates, and SIPP utility-to-following-outcome person-month records

observations.period: 2024; EIA Residential Energy Consumption Survey household energy insecurity
observations.method: EIA RECS Table HC11.1 as summarized in the retained local layer.
observations.uncertainty: Conditions can overlap and are not sequential; a notice is not a completed shutoff and the table does not identify duration, cause, or remedy.
observations.subgroup: Primary-residence housing units with published income, children, tenure, age, and race/ethnicity cells.
observations.counterinterpretation: Some households may preserve service through assistance, payment, borrowing, informal support, or a change in use.

observations.period: FY2024; LIHEAP reach and restoration aggregates

denominator.unit: HHS/ACF annual-report aggregate; household-level denominator not disclosed

observations.method: Official HHS/ACF FY2024 LIHEAP annual-report summary.
observations.uncertainty: Reach and restoration are separate program endpoints; no benefit amount, timing, prevention denominator, restoration duration, next-bill status, or repeat-crisis linkage is disclosed.
observations.subgroup: LIHEAP-assisted individuals, families, heating-assistance households, and reported restoration instances.
observations.counterinterpretation: Restoration can interrupt an immediate loss while arrears, equipment, or repeat affordability problems persist.

observations.period: 2024; SIPP utility difficulty followed by food, housing, and resource screens

denominator.unit: same-person monthly transition records; outcome cells retain separate valid denominators

observations.method: Existing SIPP November-to-December utility/care/following-outcome bridge with replicate-weight checks.
observations.uncertainty: Reference-period fields may repeat across months; no dated bill, assistance receipt, provider, shutoff, or causal counterfactual is observed.
observations.subgroup: Selected SIPP person-month pairs with utility difficulty and valid following outcome fields.
observations.counterinterpretation: Utility difficulty may reflect income, housing, health, household composition, equipment, or reporting changes; following hardship is not proof of utility causation.

related_sources.claim: EIA household consequences, service threats, sacrifice, and equipment boundaries.
LIHEAP reach and reported restoration remain separate public-system endpoints.
SIPP provides the utility-to-following-outcome descriptive transition screen.

boundary: This deliberately non-pooled synthesis separates household energy consequences, public program reach/restoration, and SIPP following outcomes. It does not estimate a causal price effect, LIHEAP take-up or restoration rate, durable recovery, health effect, trust change, or political action. A dated household bill/notice linked to assistance, reconnection, next bill, and later outcome remains open.
